nodes.name: Creosote bush
nodes.desc: The dominant shrub on gravelly desert flats across the Chihuahuan Desert. Doves and finches are recorded eating its seeds.

nodes.name: Lechuguilla
nodes.desc: A spiky agave that Wikipedia names as an indicator plant of the Chihuahuan Desert. The park's famous Lechuguilla Cave is named after it.

nodes.name: Tree cholla
nodes.desc: A tall branching cactus of desert slopes and flats. Cholla and prickly pear are a major food of woodrats.

nodes.name: Apache plume
nodes.desc: A shrub of rocky desert slopes and canyons, recorded in GloBI as browse for mule deer.

nodes.name: Moths
nodes.desc: Night-flying insects whose caterpillars eat desert plants. Wikipedia lists moths first among the prey of Mexican free-tailed bats.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: Browses shrubs such as Apache plume. A common large herbivore of the desert and canyons.

nodes.name: Barbary sheep (aoudad)
nodes.desc: A North African wild sheep introduced to the Southwest and heavily recorded near the park. It grazes and browses desert plants, competing with native herbivores.

nodes.name: White-toothed woodrat
nodes.desc: A packrat for which cacti, especially cholla and prickly pear, are a major part of the diet.

nodes.name: Merriam's kangaroo rat
nodes.desc: A seed-eating desert rodent that is prey for hawks and rattlesnakes in GloBI records.

nodes.name: White-winged dove
nodes.desc: One of the most recorded birds near the park. GloBI records it eating creosote bush, and hawks and snakes prey on it.

nodes.name: Mexican free-tailed bat
nodes.desc: The cave's famous summer bat colony flies out at dusk to feed on moths and other flying insects. Their guano carries insect energy into the cave.

nodes.name: Cave swallow
nodes.desc: Eats flying insects caught on the wing and nests at the cave entrance, which Audubon lists as an Important Bird Area.

nodes.name: Grasshopper mouse
nodes.desc: A carnivorous mouse that eats mostly insects and other invertebrates, plus small rodents like pocket mice.

nodes.name: Collared lizard
nodes.desc: A big-headed lizard of rocky desert ground that hunts insects and smaller lizards. Hawks and rattlesnakes eat it.

nodes.name: Swift fox
nodes.desc: A small desert fox. GloBI records it eating rodents such as brush mice and cotton rats.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Scavenges carcasses of deer, snakes and birds across the park. GloBI records many of these.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: A top aerial predator with a very wide diet in GloBI records, from kangaroo rats and lizards to rattlesnakes and bats.

nodes.name: Western diamondback rattlesnake
nodes.desc: Ambush predator that eats mostly small mammals such as kangaroo rats and woodrats, plus birds and lizards. Raptors hunt it.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong desert sun drives growth for the few plants that can handle the heat and dryness.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Most Chihuahuan Desert rain falls from late June to early October. Little else arrives, so this short wet season sets the pace of plant growth.

nodes.name: Springs & seeps
nodes.desc: Rattlesnake Springs and Oak Spring are rare permanent water in the park, and Rattlesnake Springs is a wooded oasis with over 300 bird species recorded.

nodes.name: Limestone desert soil
nodes.desc: Thin, rocky soil over limestone. Dead plants and animals break down slowly here and return nutrients to it.

nodes.name: Fungi, bacteria & cave insects
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, carcasses and the bat guano that builds up under roosts, returning nutrients to the soil.
